extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is introduced in the paper as an open dataset for language model pre-training. The data are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses, amount to about two trillion tokens, and include multilingual text and code across collections such as Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic.
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais; Carlos Rosas Hinostroza; Mattia Nee; Catherine Amett; Pavel Chizhov; Eliot Krzystof Jones; Irène Girard; David Mach; Anastasia Stasenko; Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.citeAs: Langlais, Pierre-Carl; Rosas Hinostroza, Carlos; Nee, Mattia; Amett, Catherine; Chizhov, Pavel; Jones, Eliot Krzystof; Girard, Irène; Mach, David; Stasenko, Anastasia; Yamshchikov, Ivan P. 2025. Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus was assembled as an aggregation of multiple open-data collections. Open Culture was compiled largely from Collections As Data dumps and otherwise collected on a resource-by-resource basis using APIs and other standard retrieval methods; Open Science was built by filtering OpenAlex by license and adding direct extractions such as arXiv and European-specific resources; Open Code uses code data from the Stack v1 and v2; Open Web includes Wikimedia projects, YouTube transcripts, and StackExchange reused from The Pile; Open Semantic adds Wikidata adapted through a collaboration with Wikimedia Deutschland.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Document analysis; Web API; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data include Collections As Data dumps of texts, datasets, PDFs, and raw XML output (METS/ALTO); OpenAlex metadata and linked original resources generally in PDF format; code data from the Stack v1 and v2 with links to original GitHub resources; Wikimedia rendered HTML dumps; audio transcripts of 2,063,066 YouTube videos uploaded under CC-By; StackExchange data reused from The Pile; and Wikidata RDF triples adapted into natural language.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Celadon, a multilingual toxicity classifier, was trained from scratch on 2M annotated samples to identify toxic and harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Microsoft Presidio; Celadon; cld2; OCRoscope; OCRerrcr; OCRonos
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical public-domain texts may contain harmful language and biases, including race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, and ability bias; Open Science has less linguistic diversity, with nearly 85% of documents currently available in English
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data; the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow; the amount of collected data (2 trillion tokens) is suitable for pre-training of models of limited size, while larger models will require significantly larger amounts of data; it does not contain data for instruction-tuning and specialized tasks and is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning; none of the curation methods could facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The release is presented as enabling open LLM research and development while meeting legal and regulatory requirements and supporting open science infrastructure; the paper also discusses risks from harmful and biased content in training data, noting that training on historical texts would lead to the reproduction and circulation of harmful language
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally identifiable information is removed from the datasets; to identify and replace PII, the authors use Microsoft Presidio and replace PII with fictitious but realistic values
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: language model pre-training; developing fully open and auditable LLMs; multimodal datasets, classifiers, synthetic datasets, and benchmarks; developing vision-language models for advanced document segmentation and processing; developing language models with legal knowledge and models for document processing in official administrative applications; training models for creative writing; development of historical language models; coding applications; improving model performance on natural language reasoning, world knowledge tasks, mathematics, and structured output tasks
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the public domain training data, they identify documents containing harmful language and either remove it or synthetically rewrite the document without the harmful language; for Wikidata, items and properties are translated into formal natural language sequences without textual synthesis, e.g., “Q41309 | P:27 | Q171150” becoming “Franz Liszt country of citizenship Kingdom of Hungary.”
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The paper describes multiple preprocessing steps: text segmentation using Segmentext; OCR error detection with OCRoscope and OCRerrcr; OCR correction with OCRonos to correct OCR errors, wrong word cuts or merges, and broken text structures; PII removal using Microsoft Presidio with custom regular expressions and replacement of PII with fictitious but realistic values; and, for Open Code, removing files not in desired languages and formats by file extension, filtering licenses to keep only permissible ones, applying manual low-quality filters, removing files with 75% or more digits, and replacing sequences of [\r]+\n with \n before recalculating line lengths.
